svg.title: Edge E3 — RV32 four-stage pipeline and parallel ASIC hardware threads
svg.desc: Textbook-style datapath with IFU frontend and separate IF-stage Predecode, IF/ID, ID/EX, EX/WB registers, operand and result multiplexers, integer ALU including a Mul/div functional group, a separate CSR block and Branch unit, and LSU. FPU omitted. Captured GPR commands fork Tensor, DMA, ACTU and CMPU work; sync retains scalar EX ownership until target completion.
svg.text: single issue · in order · EX owns variable-latency work

g.title: A 32-bit program counter. IF fetches the next instruction; an EX branch redirect changes the fetch direction.

edge_32_frontend owns one outstanding fetch, a two-entry PC/inst/error parcel FIFO, capacity/ready, start/stop and redirect cancellation. Predecode is separately instantiated in the same IF stage. I-cache sits outside the imem interface; PC, +4 and next-PC expand frontend functions for readability.

On if_id_fire, IF/ID captures the instruction-matched if_pc, if_inst and if_error. PC comes from the parcel FIFO, rather than the current fetch request. There is no separately captured PC+4 field. The bar summarizes stage ownership.

edge_32_issue_decode consumes the instruction, the IF-predecoded destination index and register classification retained by IF/ID. It produces id_issue_control and immediate. rd travels in issue_control_t for EX RAW checks and later WB. uses_gpr selects operand use; no separate Control module is implied.

IF supplies both GPR read addresses; the read-port owner captures if_rs1/if_rs2 on if_accept. Decoder use_rs1/use_rs2 controls value-or-zero selection after reading. This selection is grouped inside the symbol for readability, but RTL applies it during EX capture. Read addresses are not masked. WB forwarding remains active.
ID/EX captures the instruction, operands and issue controls. EX retains instruction ownership during multicycle operations and pending sync requests.

This functional group contains integer arithmetic, logic and RV32M multiplication/division. RTL still instantiates separate edge_32_alu and edge_32_muldiv_asap7 leaves. Multicycle operations retain EX ownership. Branch has its own block.

The CSR/counter functional group consumes captured CSR controls, rs1 or uimm and produces CSR, cycle and instret results. State changes commit in WB. This symbol does not imply a separate RTL leaf. Link values bypass it.
The branch unit consumes EX PC, rs1, rs2 and immediate, computes the condition and target, and redirects IF. It is separate from the ALU/Mul-div functional group.
The EX-owned LSU executes scalar loads and stores. Request/response interfaces connect it to D-cache and DTCM/SRAM; address routing selects the memory path.

EX sends accel_req_inst and captured operands. The product connects accel_req_src1 to req_capture_value, zero-extending a 32-bit GPR onto the 64-bit transport. The instruction completes only after accel_resp_valid.
Completed EX results transfer to WB. A pending sync response retains the instruction in EX; instructions already in WB may still retire.
WB commits architectural state and retires instructions in order. GPR writeback also supports WB-to-ID forwarding.
The product carries scalar_accel_req_inst and connects accel_req_src1 to req_capture_value. This parameter belongs to the accepted instruction; it is not a later register-file read.
edge_lite_accel_dispatch connects the command bridge and edge_accel_pipe to decode configuration, start and sync operations. This command path does not claim another fixed four-stage CPU pipeline.

Opcode/subop routes commands to their target. set_* updates configuration; start submits a stable work descriptor. Start may wait for capacity or a launch response, without waiting for the whole computation.

Target-specific sync uses tensor_sync_stall, dma_sync_done, actu_sync_stall or cmpu_sync_stall. Until the condition permits a response, EX retains the instruction. Engines keep executing during the wait.

The E3 8-by-8 tensor engine progresses independently after launch and maintains active/pending work state. Hardware thread here means an execution engine, rather than an ISA hart with its own PC and GPRs.

DMA moves data independently and may overlap scalar and engine work. RV32 commands combine low/high 32-bit values into 64-bit DMA addresses. Dependencies, memory ports and arbitration constrain overlap.
ACTU progresses independently after configuration and start. Target-specific sync waits for earlier ACTU work to drain. Shared resources remain subject to platform arbitration.
CMPU has its own start-ready and sync-stall state for independent comparison/reduction work. A target-specific sync joins it with scalar execution.

g.aria-label: Shared DTCM / SRAM fabric: inspect block
g.title: The diagram abstracts DTCM, weights and I/O storage as a shared fabric. Software must respect data dependencies; hardware still arbitrates ports and ownership.
g.text: Tensor data / weights / psum · DMA · ACTU / CMPU · arbitration & visibility

g.title: IF edge_32_decode and edge_32_register_decode produce classification, legality, unmasked GPR indices and if_write_rd. Register metadata crosses IF/ID on if_id_fire and feeds issue decode. Instruction-matched if_pc comes directly from the IFU parcel FIFO. No additional stage boundary separates IFU and Predecode.
The IFU imem request/response boundary connects to I-cache and its adapter in the cached core. Cache data/tag arrays are outside the IF frontend.
Address routing and the D-cache adapter connect LSU to cached memory. This small block denotes the external request/response boundary, matching the I-cache/imem notation above IFU.

The scalar LSU direct DTCM/SRAM route. edge_32_dtcm_router selects DTCM or cache using configured regions; the E3 platform connects the selected path to SRAM. This is the scalar entry into the shared memory fabric.
Operand A selects captured rs1 or PC according to the instruction. The symbol summarizes selection within the ALU functional group.
Operand B selects captured rs2 or immediate. Mul/div uses the two captured GPR operands. The symbol represents inputs to the functional group.
Selects completed EX results for EX/WB: LSU load, integer ALU/Mul-div, CSR/counter or link value. Only the main integer paths are expanded.
The sequential fetch path advances by four bytes. PC+4 also supplies a link value. Frontend buffering is abstracted in this view.

Selects sequential PC+4 or the EX branch redirect target. Fetch-PC+4 stays in the lower next-PC path; IF/ID separately captures the instruction-matched parcel PC. The frontend also owns buffering, hold and redirect control.

completion.svh combines ex_immediate_complete_q, is_instret && instret_read_ready_q, is_muldiv && mul_started_q && mul_result_valid, memory-class && mem_started_q && lsu_done, accel_done, cache_done, fence_i_done and ex_decode_fault_q to produce ex_release_ready. Completion requires its class/started guards. Ordinary ALU, Branch and most CSR operations use the immediate path. No extra branch_done is implied. FPU completion is outside this view.

The ID dependency/admission group consumes gpr_stall, CSR hazards, EX valid/release_ready, WB pending/header state and pipeline_kill. It produces if_ready, if_id_fire and id_capture_enable. An empty ID slot can fill while EX is busy. RAW comparison belongs to the GPR read-port owner; this is distributed logic.
